articles.summary: Hurricane Isaias weakened into a post-tropical cyclone Saturday after making landfall along Florida’s Gulf Coast, but not before the storm killed at least two people, damaged homes, and knocked out electricity for hundreds of thousands of people across the Southeast. The storm made landfall near Destin, Florida, on Friday evening as a Category 2 hurricane, packing maximum sustained winds of 105 mph. It moved north through the Florida Panhandle and into Alabama, where its winds weakened sharply. By early Saturday, Isaias had maximum sustained winds of about 35 mph, according to the National Hurricane Center . At least two people were killed when trees fell on their homes, one in Florida and another in Alabama, authorities said. The Escambia County Sheriff’s Office in Florida reported that a woman died when a tree struck her home. In Jefferson County, Alabama, emergency management officials reported a second fatality after a tree fell on a house. Officials had not released further details about the victims. The storm also caused widespread damage across the Florida Panhandle and southern Alabama. Strong winds toppled trees and power lines, damaged buildings, and left roads hazardous.

articles.summary: Before the mid-19th century, executions in America were presumptively public. Most prisoners were hanged on a gallows, following an hours-long affair that began with the condemned person’s exit from jail accompanied by ministers, the sheriff and his deputies, and sometimes a military escort. Spectators joined the humiliating procession, gathering by the thousands to watch the noose lowered over the prisoner’s neck. The sheriff would mount the scaffold to read aloud the death warrant, sometimes adding commentary, and at least one minister (often several) would issue sermons. The condemned was offered the chance to give a speech, with spectators standing so close that they could ask the prisoner questions and join him in prayer, or bid him goodbye, if he was a family member or friend. All of that seemed safely confined to a past that the Trump administration now hopes to revive. President Trump, a consummate showman, has authorized the country’s first public execution in 90 years.
